source: MortalityPredictors.org Curated Prospective Mortality Database Export

records.citation: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration. C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and all-cause mortality: meta-analysis of individual participant data from 54 long-term prospective studies. Lancet. 2010;375(9710):132-140.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, diabetes, BMI
records.notes: Meta-analysis across 54 prospective studies demonstrating strong log-linear association with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

records.citation: Ridker PM, et al. C-Reactive Protein and Other Markers of Inflammation in the Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease in Women. N Engl J Med. 2000;342(12):836-843.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, lipid levels, BMI
records.notes: Highest quartile of CRP associated with elevated risk of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality.

records.citation: Goldwasser P, Feldman J. Association of serum albumin and mortality risk. J Clin Epidemiol. 1997;50(6):693-703.
records.cohort_description: Systematic Review of General and Hospitalized Cohorts
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, baseline comorbidities, inflammation, nutritional markers
records.notes: Strong inverse association between serum albumin concentration and mortality; lower albumin signifies chronic inflammation, liver synthetic decline, or protein-energy wasting.

records.citation: Phillips A, Shaper AG, Whincup PH. Association between serum albumin and mortality from cardiovascular disease, cancer, and other causes. Lancet. 1989;2(8677):1434-1436.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, smoking, blood pressure, cholesterol, pre-existing CVD
records.notes: Men in lowest quintile of serum albumin (<42 g/L) had significantly increased mortality from all causes.

records.citation: Patel KV, et al. Red cell distribution width and mortality in older adults: a meta-analysis. Arch Intern Med. 2009;169(6):588-594.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, education, cardiovascular disease, cancer, hemoglobin, MCV
records.notes: Higher RDW strongly predicts all-cause mortality in older adults, even in the absence of anemia or microcytosis.

records.citation: Perlstein TS, et al. Red cell distribution width and mortality in risk of cardiovascular and all-cause mortality: NHANES III. Arch Intern Med. 2009;169(6):588-594.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, smoking, diabetes, hypertension, blood lipids, eGFR, CRP
records.notes: Highest quartile vs lowest quartile of RDW confers 72% higher risk of death after extensive multivariable adjustment.

records.citation: Astor BC, et al. Association of kidney function measures with mortality and end-stage renal disease in individuals with and without hypertension: a meta-analysis. Lancet. 2011;377(9765):577-584.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, systolic blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, history of CVD, total cholesterol
records.notes: Elevated serum creatinine with reduced filtration rate is a potent driver of both cardiovascular and all-cause mortality.

records.citation: Xie Y, et al. Blood urea nitrogen is associated with all-cause mortality: prospective cohort of 1.3 million US veterans. Kidney Int. 2018;93(4):874-885.
records.cohort_description: US Department of Veterans Affairs National Cohort
records.adjustment_covariates: eGFR, age, sex, race, BMI, diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, medications
records.notes: Independent relationship between blood urea nitrogen and all-cause mortality across all stages of estimated GFR.

records.citation: Bleys J, et al. Serum uric acid and cardiovascular and all-cause mortality: a prospective study in NHANES III. Arch Intern Med. 2007;167(4):404-410.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, education, smoking, alcohol, BMI, physical activity, hypertension, diabetes, total cholesterol, eGFR
records.notes: High uric acid is associated with increased all-cause and cardiovascular mortality independent of traditional risk factors.

records.citation: Cho SK, et al. U-shaped association between serum uric acid and all-cause mortality in Korean adults. Korean J Intern Med. 2018;33(5):984-992.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, BMI, smoking status, alcohol intake, exercise, glucose, lipids, blood pressure
records.notes: U-shaped curve observed where both hypouricemia (<3.5 mg/dL) and hyperuricemia (>7.5 mg/dL) had elevated mortality risk.

records.citation: Kunutsor SK, et al. Alkaline phosphatase and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. Eur J Epidemiol. 2014;29(5):309-324.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, conventional cardiovascular risk factors, liver enzymes, renal function
records.notes: Linear dose-response association between elevated circulating ALP and increased risk of all-cause and cardiovascular death.

records.citation: Kunutsor SK, et al. Gamma-glutamyltransferase and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. Eur J Epidemiol. 2014;29(6):381-392.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, alcohol intake, BMI, smoking, physical activity, blood lipids, glucose, blood pressure
records.notes: GGT exhibits strong linear association with vascular and all-cause mortality, reflecting hepatic steatosis and oxidative stress.

records.citation: Boffetta P, et al. Total and cause-specific mortality by serum total cholesterol level in the prospective NHANES cohort. Ann Epidemiol. 2011;21(3):174-182.
records.cohort_description: NHANES I, II, and III Pooled Follow-up Cohorts
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, education, smoking, body mass index, diabetes, hypertension
records.notes: U-shaped relationship: low cholesterol (<160 mg/dL) associated with non-CVD death, high cholesterol (>240 mg/dL) associated with CVD death.

records.citation: Campbell F, et al. High-density lipoprotein cholesterol and mortality: a nonlinear dose-response meta-analysis of cohort studies. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2021;78(2):142-154.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, alcohol, BMI, blood pressure, diabetes, lipid-lowering drugs
records.notes: U-shaped association with nadir of risk around 55-65 mg/dL; both very low (<35 mg/dL) and extremely high (>90 mg/dL) HDL-C increase mortality.

records.citation: Johannesen CDL, et al. Association between low density lipoprotein and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in Denmark: prospective cohort study. BMJ. 2020;371:m4266.
records.cohort_description: Copenhagen General Population Study & Copenhagen City Heart Study
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, physical activity, alcohol, education, diabetes, statin use
records.notes: U-shaped risk in general population cohorts with lowest mortality at 140 mg/dL in untreated individuals and strong CVD risk in top decile.

records.citation: Sarwar N, et al. Triglycerides and the risk of coronary heart disease and all-cause mortality: 10,158 incident cases among 262,525 participants in 29 Western prospective studies. Circulation. 2007;115(4):450-458.
records.cohort_description: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration (29 Prospective Studies)
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, total cholesterol, HDL-C, SBP, BMI, diabetes
records.notes: Elevated triglycerides independently associate with increased cardiovascular and all-cause mortality.

records.citation: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration. Diabetes mellitus, fasting blood glucose concentration, and risk of vascular disease: a collaborative meta-analysis of 102 prospective studies. Lancet. 2010;375(9733):2215-2222.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking status, systolic blood pressure, BMI, total cholesterol
records.notes: Fasting glucose >100 mg/dL is associated with linear increases in vascular and total mortality risk.

records.citation: Currie CJ, et al. Survival as a function of HbA1c in people with type 2 diabetes: a retrospective cohort study. Lancet. 2010;375(9713):481-489.
records.cohort_description: UK General Practice Research Database (GPRD) Cohort
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, cholesterol, blood pressure, cardiovascular comorbidities, diabetes therapy
records.notes: U-shaped relationship: HbA1c nadir at ~7.0-7.5% in diabetics, with elevated mortality at both <6.5% and >9.0%.

records.citation: Lee CD, et al. Total and differential white blood cell counts, cardiovascular disease, and mortality in middle-aged men and women: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study. Atherosclerosis. 2001;154(3):729-736.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, LDL-C, HDL-C, BMI
records.notes: Highest quintile of WBC count (>7.5 x 10^3/uL) had 44% elevated risk of all-cause mortality compared to lowest quintile.

records.citation: Zakai NA, et al. A prospective study of anemia and all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older adults: the Cardiovascular Health Study. Arch Intern Med. 2005;165(19):2214-2220.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, smoking, eGFR, heart failure, stroke, coronary disease, diabetes, CRP
records.notes: Both anemia (<12 g/dL in women, <13 g/dL in men) and elevated polycythemic hemoglobin levels (>17 g/dL) associate with mortality.

records.citation: Vinholt PJ, et al. Platelet count is associated with all-cause mortality in the general population: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Thromb Haemost. 2016;115(5):981-990.
records.cohort_description: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of General Population Cohorts
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, malignancy, baseline medications
records.notes: U-shaped association: both thrombocytopenia (<150 x 10^3/uL) and reactive thrombocytosis (>350 x 10^3/uL) carry increased risk.

records.citation: Chronic Kidney Disease Prognosis Consortium. Association of estimated glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in general population cohorts: a collaborative meta-analysis. Lancet. 2010;375(9731):2073-2081.
records.cohort_description: CKD Prognosis Consortium (1.05 Million Adults Across 21 Cohorts)
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, systolic blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, total cholesterol, eGFR
records.notes: Linear logarithmic increase in mortality beginning even at microalbuminuria levels (>10 mg/g).

records.citation: He J, et al. 24-Hour urinary creatinine excretion and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in the chronic renal insufficiency cohort. Am J Kidney Dis. 2014;63(4):618-626.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, BMI, proteinuria, eGFR, systolic BP, diabetes, cardiovascular disease
records.notes: Lower urinary creatinine excretion reflects diminished muscle mass / sarcopenia and independently predicts premature death.

records.citation: Perrier ET, et al. Relation of spot urine specific gravity and hydration status to all-cause mortality in US adults: NHANES analysis. Eur J Clin Nutr. 2017;71(12):1428-1433.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, BMI, physical activity, alcohol, smoking, hypertension, diabetes, renal function
records.notes: Both extreme hyposthenuria (<1.010) and severe hypersthenuria (>1.025) predict elevated mortality.

records.citation: Sontrop JM, et al. Association between volume of urine output and mortality in community-dwelling adults. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2013;8(11):1948-1956.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, baseline eGFR, diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular history
records.notes: Oliguria and severe polyuria both indicate physiological distress, electrolyte imbalance, or impaired renal concentrating ability.

records.citation: Garland CF, et al. Meta-analysis of all-cause mortality according to serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Am J Public Health. 2014;104(8):e43-e50.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, latitude, season, BMI, physical activity, smoking
records.notes: Subjects with circulating 25(OH)D <20 ng/mL exhibit significantly higher mortality than those in the 30-50 ng/mL range.

records.citation: Rapsomaniki E, et al. Blood pressure and risk of vascular disease: 1.25 million people from the CALIBER study. Lancet. 2014;383(9932):1899-1911.
records.cohort_description: CALIBER UK Electronic Health Records Linked Cohort
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, diabetes, total cholesterol, HDL, antihypertensive medications
records.notes: Continuous graded increase in cardiovascular and total mortality risk starting from SBP >115 mmHg.

records.citation: Lewington S, et al. Age-specific relevance of usual blood pressure to vascular mortality: a meta-analysis of individual data for one million adults in 61 prospective studies. Lancet. 2002;360(9349):1903-1913.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, cholesterol, smoking status
records.notes: Each 10 mmHg higher DBP is associated with approximately 20-30% increase in cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk in middle age.

records.citation: Fox CS, et al. Resting heart rate and risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality: the Framingham Heart Study. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2008;52(15):1258-1264.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, systolic BP, diabetes, smoking, total/HDL cholesterol ratio, BMI, physical activity
records.notes: Resting heart rate reflects autonomic nervous balance; higher RHR is an independent predictor of all-cause and cardiovascular death.

records.citation: Zhang D, et al. Resting heart rate and all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in the general population: a meta-analysis. CMAJ. 2016;188(3):E53-E63.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, physical activity, blood pressure, cholesterol, BMI
records.notes: Every 10 bpm increase in resting heart rate confers a 9% higher risk of all-cause mortality and 8% higher risk of CVD mortality.

records.citation: Kaptoge S, et al. Interleukin-6 and risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and all-cause mortality: prospective cohort studies meta-analysis. Eur Heart J. 2014;35(9):578-589.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, lipid profile, BMI, diabetes
records.notes: Circulating IL-6 upstream driver of acute-phase proteins with strong linear hazard for all-cause death.

records.citation: Cesari M, et al. Inflammatory markers and cardiovascular disease (The Health ABC Study). Circulation. 2003;108(19):2317-2322.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, BMI, physical activity, smoking, blood pressure, medications
records.notes: Elevated TNF-alpha predicts incident cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality in aging populations.

records.citation: Fibrinogen Studies Collaboration. Plasma fibrinogen level and the risk of major cardiovascular diseases and non-vascular mortality. JAMA. 2005;294(14):1799-1809.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, cholesterol, blood pressure, BMI, diabetes
records.notes: Plasma fibrinogen is a key coagulation and inflammatory protein with continuous graded mortality risk.

records.citation: Shlipak MG, et al. Cystatin C versus creatinine in determining risk based on kidney function. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(10):932-943.
records.cohort_description: CKD Prognosis Consortium (11 General Population Cohorts)
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, cardiovascular disease, BMI, albuminuria
records.notes: Cystatin C outperforms serum creatinine as a predictor of all-cause and cardiovascular death.

records.citation: Matsushita K, et al. Association of estimated glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in general population cohorts. Lancet. 2010;375(9731):2073-2081.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, history of cardiovascular disease, SBP, diabetes, smoking, total cholesterol, albuminuria
records.notes: eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73m2 exhibits steep exponential increases in all-cause mortality.

records.citation: Sniderman AD, et al. Apolipoprotein B particles and cardiovascular risk: a comprehensive meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies. JAMA Cardiol. 2019;4(12):1287-1295.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, BMI, statin use
records.notes: ApoB measures the exact particle number of all atherogenic lipoproteins and is superior to LDL-C for predicting vascular death.

records.citation: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration. Major lipids, apolipoproteins, and risk of vascular disease. JAMA. 2009;302(18):1993-2000.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, systolic BP, diabetes, body mass index
records.notes: ApoA1 is the principal protein of anti-atherogenic HDL particles; higher levels protect against vascular and all-cause death.

records.citation: Erqou S, et al. Lipoprotein(a) concentration and the risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and nonvascular mortality. JAMA. 2009;302(4):412-423.
records.cohort_description: Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration (36 Prospective Studies)
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, lipids, diabetes
records.notes: Genetically determined pro-thrombotic and pro-atherogenic particle; levels above 50 mg/dL independently increase mortality.

records.citation: Ausmanas M, et al. Fasting insulin and long-term mortality: a 20-year prospective cohort study. Diabetologia. 2012;55(9):2340-2348.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, BMI, blood pressure, smoking, physical activity, cholesterol
records.notes: Hyperinsulinemia indicates systemic insulin resistance and endothelial stress.

records.citation: Hedblad B, et al. Insulin resistance in relation to incidence of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality: the Malmo Diet and Cancer Study. Diabetologia. 2002;45(5):638-644.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, physical activity, waist circumference, blood pressure, lipids
records.notes: Homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance is a strong predictor of metabolic dysfunction and mortality.

records.citation: Kunutsor SK, et al. Liver enzymes and risk of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Epidemiol. 2014;29(5):309-324.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, alcohol consumption, viral hepatitis markers, BMI, smoking
records.notes: U-shaped relationship: low ALT signals sarcopenia and hepatic frailty; elevated ALT reflects hepatosteatosis.

records.citation: Ruhl CE, Everhart JE. Elevated serum alanine and aspartate aminotransferase and mortality in the United States. Gastroenterology. 2009;136(2):477-485.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, alcohol, viral hepatitis, diabetes, BMI, physical activity
records.notes: Elevated AST is a marker of hepatocellular necrosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and toxic liver injury.

records.citation: Horsfall LJ, et al. Serum bilirubin and risk of cardiovascular disease, cancer, and mortality: a cohort study in UK primary care. Lancet. 2011;377(9763):414-420.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, alcohol, BMI, blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes
records.notes: Endogenous antioxidant; moderately higher physiological bilirubin is protective against CVD and all-cause death.

records.citation: Ellervik C, et al. Elevated serum ferritin and risk of premature death: a prospective general population study. J Intern Med. 2014;275(4):379-390.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, alcohol, BMI, CRP, liver enzymes, diabetes
records.notes: Iron storage and acute-phase protein; both severe iron deficiency and iron overload/inflammation increase mortality.

records.citation: Erikssen G, et al. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: a possible marker of atherosclerosis and a strong predictor of coronary heart disease and mortality. Eur Heart J. 2000;21(19):1614-1620.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, physical fitness, blood pressure, lipids, smoking
records.notes: Classic non-specific systemic inflammatory and rheological marker that predicts long-term vascular and cancer death.

records.citation: Fest J, et al. The systemic inflammation markers NLR and PLR and all-cause mortality: the Rotterdam Study. Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev. 2018;27(7):735-741.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, alcohol, BMI, diabetes, hypertension, lipid medications
records.notes: Reflects balance between innate inflammatory activation (neutrophils) and adaptive immune senescence (lymphocytes).

records.citation: Waikar SS, et al. Serum sodium and risk of death in the US population: NHANES III analysis. Am J Med. 2011;124(8):777-784.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, heart failure, cirrhosis, kidney disease, hypertension, diuretics
records.notes: Both hyponatremia (<135 mmol/L) and hypernatremia (>145 mmol/L) are potent markers of dysregulated fluid homeostasis and mortality.

records.citation: Krogager C, et al. Potassium and mortality in general and clinical populations: a systematic review. Am J Cardiovasc Drugs. 2017;17(4):287-299.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, renal function, heart failure, ACE inhibitors, diuretics, arrhythmias
records.notes: Strict physiological homeostatic band (4.0-4.8 mmol/L); hypokalemia causes lethal arrhythmias and hyperkalemia causes cardiac arrest.

records.citation: Foley RN, et al. Serum calcium and phosphorus levels and mortality in the US general population: NHANES III. Kidney Int. 2009;76(7):767-772.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, race, eGFR, albumin, phosphorus, PTH, vitamin D, smoking, hypertension
records.notes: Albumin-adjusted serum calcium demonstrates a U-shaped association with cardiovascular and all-cause death.

records.citation: Tonelli M, et al. Relation between serum phosphate levels and cardiovascular events in people with and without chronic kidney disease. Circulation. 2005;112(17):2627-2633.
records.cohort_description: CARE Trial Cohort with Normal and Mildly Reduced Renal Function
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, baseline eGFR, cholesterol, diabetes, blood pressure, smoking
records.notes: Serum phosphate promotes medial vascular calcification and arterial stiffness even in individuals with normal renal function.

records.citation: Natriuretic Peptides Studies Collaboration. Natriuretic peptides and risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality: a prospective meta-analysis of individual participant data. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2016;4(12):1004-1016.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, smoking, blood pressure, cholesterol, BMI, eGFR, diabetes, prior CVD
records.notes: Myocardial wall tension marker; potent predictor of heart failure, stroke, and all-cause mortality.

records.citation: Willeit P, et al. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin T and risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality in the general population: a meta-analysis. Circulation. 2017;135(7):642-656.
records.cohort_description: Meta-analysis of 28 Prospective General Population Cohorts
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, conventional cardiovascular risk factors, eGFR, NT-proBNP
records.notes: Subclinical myocardial injury marker; even minor elevations within the normal range indicate heightened mortality risk.

records.citation: Leong DP, et al. Prognostic value of grip strength: findings from the Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE) study. Lancet. 2015;386(9990):266-273.
records.cohort_description: PURE Prospective Cohort (17 High-, Middle-, Low-Income Countries)
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, education, physical activity, tobacco, alcohol, diet, BMI, blood pressure, diabetes
records.notes: Handgrip strength is a robust biomarker of generalized muscular fitness and neuromuscular reserve; superior to SBP in predicting all-cause death.

records.citation: Mandsager K, et al. Association of cardiorespiratory fitness with long-term mortality among adults undergoing exercise treadmill testing. JAMA Netw Open. 2018;1(6):e183605.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, height, weight, BMI, resting HR, resting BP, medications, history of CAD, diabetes, smoking
records.notes: Cardiorespiratory fitness has an inverse, monotonic, non-plateauing association with all-cause mortality; elite fitness has the lowest risk.

records.citation: Vlachopoulos C, et al. Prediction of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality with arterial stiffness: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2010;55(13):1318-1327.
records.adjustment_covariates: Age, sex, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, cholesterol, diabetes, smoking
records.notes: Aortic pulse wave velocity measures central arterial wall elastance and stiffness; strongly predicts premature vascular death.
